encoding_notes: Publisher verified: Elsevier on ScienceDirect, official journal of OARSI; no publisher migration. Submission via Editorial Manager (editorialmanager.com/OAC).

Live page 403-blocked to plain WebFetch and Wayback host blocked to WebFetch; full live guide text obtained via headless-browser scrape (Apify rag-web-browser). Content is live/clean, not a shell — treated as TIER_A but flagged headless/blocked for cron.

references.style set to 'custom': the guide says 'consult the AMA Manual of Style (ed. 8)' for general style, but the reference-list EXAMPLES are the Elsevier numbered format (initials-before-surname, journal names abbreviated per ISSN LTWA, DOI included) which is not classic AMA/Vancouver.

journal_abbrev='nlm' is an approximation: the guide specifies the ISSN List of Title Word Abbreviations (LTWA), not NLM specifically, but titles ARE abbreviated (not full), and the schema only offers nlm|full.

SCHEMA GAP - combined figure+table caps: full-length original research = 'no more than 4000 words, 8 figures and tables, and 50 references'; reviews = 'max 8 tables and/or figures, 100 references'; brief report = '2 figures and/or tables'; editorial/commentary = 'max 2 figures and/or tables'. These are COMBINED figure+table limits; figures_max/tables_max left null (per-type) to avoid implying separate caps. Full-length & reviews combined cap = 8; editorial combined cap = 2.

Article-type mapping: 'Full length original research article' -> original_research; 'Narrative Reviews' -> narrative_review; 'Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses' -> systematic_review; 'Editorial and Commentary' -> editorial; 'Letter to the editor' -> letter.

OMITTED type: 'Brief report of original research' (abstract 250 words, main text 2000 words, 15 references, 2 figures/tables) has no clean enum slot distinct from original_research, so it is not encoded as its own key. Its limits are noted here for reference.
Letter to the editor: 800 words, no abstract, no tables or figures, max 8 references (encoded abstract_max_words=0, figures_max=0, tables_max=0).

Abstract is required and structured (Objective; Design; Results; Conclusions) for all relevant types INCLUDING narrative reviews and systematic reviews; max 350 words. Keywords: 3-6, English spelling; case/separator unstated.
line_numbers='continuous' and page_numbers.show=true from: 'Number each page sequentially and add line numbers, including the title page, abstract, text, references, figure legends, and tables.'
Font, size, line spacing, margins, page size, alignment, first-line indent, heading formatting: all UNSTATED in the guide -> null.

separate_title_page=true: submission requires a separate file containing title page + abstract, with the main-text file excluding the title page and abstract. No instruction to scrub author identifiers from the body -> scrub_body_identifiers=false; peer review described as 'internally and/or externally' with no double-blind/anonymized statement -> double_blind=false.

cover_letter_required=true inferred from: 'Approvals ... must be explicitly stated in the submission cover letter' (ethics approvals) plus Mendelian-Randomisation cover-letter rationale requirement; the guide treats the cover letter as a required submission component.

declarations.required lists universally-required statements (author contributions, funding/role of funding source, competing interests). ethics_approval and patient_consent are required only when human/animal subjects are involved (Section 4). data_availability/Data statement is 'encouraged', not required, so it is in order but not in required.

tables.placement='grouped_end': suggested position marked in text, but each table typed on a separate page; table legends typed ABOVE each table (caption_position='above'); Arabic numbering for both figures and tables.
figures.formats: guide lists 'BMP, TIF, or PDF' as readily-available formats and states JPG/PPT lack sufficient detail; encoded ['tif','pdf'] (BMP has no enum slot). No DPI value stated.
orcid_required=true: title page must include ORCID ID for each co-author.
